title: Tell agents to fill in priority and estimate fields when filing items
lead: Agent guidance for creating roadmap items never asks for importance, urgency, effort, size, tree or findings, so agent-filed items land at the defaults and the roadmap cannot be sorted until someone scores them by hand.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Every item defaults to importance 2, urgency 2 and no effort, and `list`, `next` and `sort` rank on those fields. At the start of the 2026-09-29 v1.0.0 triage, all six open items in this repo scored 32 with no quadrant, so the queue order carried no information and a separate pass was needed to score them. The agent-facing text does not prompt for these fields: the "Plan and record agreed work" section of `slicer ai instructions` (`src/slicer/ai.py`, `INSTRUCTIONS`) shows `slicer add "Title" --render --json` with only `--depends-on`, and the "Convert an agreed roadmap" prompt in `docs/agents.md` asks for importance and urgency but not `effort`, `size`, `tree` or `findings`. `slicer import --skeleton` already lists every metadata key, so the outline path has the shape; the guidance just does not ask for it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py` (`INSTRUCTIONS`, the "Plan and record agreed work" section; `LOOP`, `EXITS` and `SPEC_GAP` are shared with `ai skill`)
- `docs/agents.md` (the "Plan a new project", "Review an existing project" and "Convert an agreed roadmap" prompts, and the agent rules)
- `tests/test_ai.py`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `ai instructions` tells an agent filing an item, by `add` or by outline, to propose `--importance`, `--urgency` and `--effort` (and `--size`, `--tree` and `--findings` where the project uses them), with a one-line reason for each score, instead of leaving the defaults.
2. Its `add` example includes those flags and still parses (the existing parser-example test).
3. The `docs/agents.md` planning and conversion prompts ask for the same fields.
4. The existing `tests/test_ai.py` guarantees still hold, and `ai skill` output is unchanged unless the shared loop is deliberately edited.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Settle with the project before building, do not infer:

- Whether the agent sets proposed values directly and reports them, or proposes them for the owner to confirm before filing.
- Whether `add` or `import --dry-run` should also warn when an item is filed at the default 2/2 with no effort. That is a tool change, not a docs change, and may belong in its own slice.

Then update the planning text and prompts. Keep the addition short: S138 is trimming the same `INSTRUCTIONS` text, so do the two together or rebase one on the other.

Settled with the owner (2026-09-29):

- The agent sets its proposed values when it files the item and reports a one-line reason for each score in its reply; the owner adjusts with `set`.
- Guidance only. A tool nudge for items filed at the default 2/2 with no effort is a separate post-1.0 item.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The tests above pass; the suite and `slicer check` pass.
